> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **149** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 15764cd723e750c01416cfe91b44bbd0a4c28f37` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f013023b84420bebd2f4dc38c20602891d7e71d5` — the merge of head `54971471cc12809500c7f7c5c3afa8e2e021892f` into base `15764cd723e750c01416cfe91b44bbd0a4c28f37`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f013023b84420bebd2f4dc38c20602891d7e71d5 && git checkout f013023b84420bebd2f4dc38c20602891d7e71d5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 15764cd723e750c01416cfe91b44bbd0a4c28f37 54971471cc12809500c7f7c5c3afa8e2e021892f && git checkout -B drift-repro 15764cd723e750c01416cfe91b44bbd0a4c28f37 && git merge --no-ff 54971471cc12809500c7f7c5c3afa8e2e021892f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 15764cd723e750c01416cfe91b44bbd0a4c28f37
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 15764cd723e750c01416cfe91b44bbd0a4c28f37` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `54971471cc12809500c7f7c5c3afa8e2e021892f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/data-driver.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-pinyin-search/src/companion-projection.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-autonumber-issue-ahead.test.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-remote-autonumber-issue-ahead.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-autonumber-stored-expression.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-pinyin-search/src/companion-autonumber-recompute.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/autonumber-stored-expression.integration.test.ts, .changeset/25073-autonumber-stored-expression.md; cited code read at the head: packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts (`DriverOptions`, `DriverInterfaceSchema`), packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts (unchanged), packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-remote-inherited-members.test.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/index.ts, packages/objectql/package.json.

Reviewed 2026-10-22T14:25Z on card #25073, ruling 6335312761 (letter A), the seat's surface call 6340248712, the cross-lane declaration on #6017 (6339724909), the dev report 6342739367, the PR body with its Acceptance notes, the net diff against the merge base `15764cd723e750c01416cfe91b44bbd0a4c28f37`, and the 42 check-runs on this head (every one `success` or path-skipped; `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` all `success`). Read-only: nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) The ruling's premise and the insert ordering — right, on every path.** At this head the insert body's second stored-expression pass (`computeStoredExpressions`, engine.ts near 17136) still runs before validation; the new issue loop sits exactly where `applyAutonumbers` already ran, after validation (near 17264), so a rejected row burns no number, in partial mode too (dead rows are skipped at issue and at recompute). `recomputeAutonumberReaders` (near 17284) then recomputes over every live row that received a number from either issuer and tells the listeners; `createWithAutonumberResync` (near 8794) recomputes after each re-issue under the same `AUTONUMBER_COLLISION_ATTEMPTS` (3); the batch door re-seeds (the engine's counters, or the member on driver-issued numbers, near 17343) and never re-issues, then throws the `DUPLICATE_RECORD` envelope — the engine's pre-existing #6806 policy, now symmetric across issuers. One retry loop: `SqlDriver.create` / `bulkCreate` find the slot filled (`fillAutoNumberFields` skips a non-empty slot) and reserve nothing, so their own #5495 retry cannot fire on a pre-issued number and the engine's loop is the only loop on that path. Row identity holds where the member needs it: `liveRows` maps to the same `rows[i]` objects the member keyed its reservations on (a weak map by row object), the collision call passes those same objects, and `create()` copies into `toInsert` only afterwards. Transitive readers: `storedExpressionsReading` closes over `record.x` reads through `analyzeRelationshipTraversals` with a fixpoint loop, counts an entry whose reads it cannot name as a reader (conservative), and `applyFormulaPlan` folds entries sequentially in plan order, so a reader-of-a-reader sees the fresh value (pinned as `headline` on fakes and on real SQLite, after a collision too). Measured on both issuers over hand-rolled drivers (objectql), on real SQLite through `SqlDriver` (runtime, including `afterInsert` and a caller transaction), and on the Turso remote face.

**(b) The `IDataDriver` member — right, optional, complete.** `issueAutonumbers?(object, rows, options?, afterCollision?)` answering a promise of per-row filled-field-name lists; `afterCollision` is `unknown`, not `any`. The TSDoc states both modes, the row-identity requirement, the typed-value and caller-transaction silences, and the two omission cases. Absence is handled on every driver class: no `supports.autonumber` (driver-memory, driver-mongodb) ⇒ the engine issues as before and now recomputes; `supports.autonumber` without the member (a third-party driver) ⇒ the number stays inside `create()` and the engine reports once per object at `error` with the consequence and the remedy — the right level by AGENTS.md's one question (the write reports success while the stored value is not what its declaration says), pinned. Detection is `typeof driver.issueAutonumbers === 'function'` plus `supports.autonumber`; no `instanceof SqlDriver`, no driver-name branch anywhere in the diff. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` names every exported change: `IDataDriver.issueAutonumbers` (spec), `SqlDriver.issueAutonumbers` (driver-sql), `ObjectQL.registerInsertRecomputeListener` (objectql), the plugin's registration (plugin-pinyin-search), and the error-code change on the exhausted path; `REMOTE_FACE_ANSWERS` is not re-exported from driver-turso's index, so its new row is internal. `hook.zod.ts` is untouched; `DriverInterfaceSchema` mirrors the core verbs only and is not widened, consistent with the other optional members. The member is declared to `domain:spec` on #6017 as ruling item 6 asks.

**(c) The `__search` route — right, in the approved family.** `registerInsertRecomputeListener(id, fn)` sits beside `registerWriteGateProbe` and `registerEffectiveObjectPermissionsResolver` on the `ObjectQL` class (none of the three is on a spec interface), keyed by registrant id so a re-bind replaces itself, feature-detected by the plugin through its `MinimalEngine` shape. No new `HookEvent` name; no package-name branch in engine code (the plugin is named only in a docblock). The plugin's listener re-stamps the companion onto the very row the driver is handed, narrowed to the recomputed fields: a companion whose source was not recomputed keeps its `beforeInsert` stamp (control pinned), an object without a companion column gets none (control pinned), it fires again on every re-issue (pinned on the engine), and `stampCompanion` never throws. `$search` finds the record by pinyin and by its number on both issuers.

**(d) The dev's deviations, each judged:**
- **(1) the `__search` extension** — inside ruling item 4 (a search column without the number is the same defect in another column, recomputed in the same write step) through the seat's call 6340248712, in the approved family, no `HookEvent`, no package-name branch; the plugin rides the one changeset at `patch`. Inside.
- **(2) the forced one-row edit to `REMOTE_FACE_ANSWERS`** (`issueAutonumbers: 'inherited'`) — forced by the table's `satisfies` clause over every key of `SqlDriver` (turso-driver.ts near 1126): a public member on `SqlDriver` is a required key and the DTS build fails without it. The value is measured right: `turso-remote-autonumber-issue-ahead.test.ts` pins not-redeclared, issue from the remote counter the remote `create()` draws from, collision re-seed to 30 and the slot emptied, `CASE-00031` next, and silence on a typed duplicate; `turso-remote-inherited-members.test.ts` holds every `inherited` row to the code. Ruling item 5 asked for exactly this measurement and named a non-inheriting face as the fork; this face inherits. Declared in the PR body and the report; #25198's region is disjoint and the merge was clean. Justified.
- **(4) "one retry loop for every driver" read as the single-row loop** — the ruling names "the engine's existing `createWithAutonumberResync`", which is the single-row loop by construction; the batch door's "re-seed, never re-issue" is the engine's pre-existing policy, now applied to driver-issued numbers through the member (re-seed by `resyncSequenceToDataMax`, stale slots emptied, batch not re-issued, the next insert past the store — pinned on fakes and on SQLite). Issuing ahead only for objects with a reader follows ruling item 1's purpose clause ("recomputes the stored fields whose expression reads an issued autonumber") and leaves every other object's path, error code and in-driver #6943 batch heal byte-identical; the literal reading would have carried the error-code change to every autonumber object with no measured producer and dropped a heal the ruling never weighed. Inside ruling A as the conservative reading, declared in the Acceptance notes. If the maintainer meant every autonumber object to issue ahead, that is a follow-up ruling, not a defect of this head.
- **(5) `ERR_AUTONUMBER_COLLISION` on an exhausted SQL collision for reader objects** — the direct consequence of ruling item 1 moving the retry into the engine's loop, whose exhaustion exit has always been this code on the engine-issued path (driver-memory, driver-mongodb); the attempt count is comparable (3 engine attempts against the driver's 4), and every object without a reader is unchanged. Inside the ruling; named as a published behaviour change in the changeset ("One change in what a refused insert reports") and in the PR body; a ledger-registered code under `@objectstack/objectql`. Level: not a metadata-protocol kind, so `patch` under AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3. Right.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-turso` and `@objectstack/plugin-pinyin-search`: all five are `private: false` and each is moved by the diff; `driver-sqlite-wasm` inherits with no diff and `runtime` moves only a test, so neither is owed one. AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 sets the level from the kind alone — `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`" — so the dispatch's `minor` conflicts with AGENTS.md, which wins. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body; the widening is a new optional contract member plus a new engine registration method, so the accept set grows and nothing an author or a driver could write is refused. `Check Changeset` is green on the head. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviations 1–4** (surface extension; forced Turso row; `patch` not `minor`; the retry-loop reading): answered in ① — each inside the ruling or settled by AGENTS.md.
- **Deviations 5 and 6** (the attribution link points at the card thread; no review request on the PR): outside the contract face; noted, nothing owed here.
- **Deviation 7** (merged `main` before the final gate rerun): the net diff is read against the merge base `15764cd7`, the local families were rerun at the merged head, and the check-runs on `54971471c` are the verdict — all green.
- **Acceptance note — validation and the RLS write seam judge the pre-number value:** by ruling items 1 and 3 (the order binds; a rejected row burns no number); no card owed.
- **Acceptance note — upsert is not covered:** the card and the ruling are the insert path. By reading, `engine.upsert` → `driver.upsert` is the same defect class on an upsert that inserts, and it is unmeasured. Escalated to the seat: probe it and file on a measured reproduction (filing gate ①); not this PR's.
- **Acceptance note — inside a caller transaction the member answers no collision:** matches the driver's own `mayRetry` today and the ruling's carried confidence gap (a caller-owned PostgreSQL transaction aborts on a failed INSERT); pinned in driver-sql's test.
- **Acceptance note — Turso remote `bulkCreate` partial application:** pre-existing and unchanged; the batch policy above is what protects it.
- **Acceptance note — a driver without the member keeps today's stored value, at `error` once per object:** right level, pinned.
- **`open_questions`: none.**
- **Test evidence:** the report gives per-file pass counts and ablation red/green pinned to this head, which reconcile with the files (objectql 2×8 + 4 = 20 with 7 green = 4 controls + member-not-asked + exhaustion + no-member; runtime 10 with 2 controls; plugin 2×5 with 4 controls); the dogfood battery is pinned to the head; the check-runs are the gate verdict.
- **Observations for the seat, not defects of this head:** (i) the `insert()` docblock (engine.ts near 16293) still says the `ERR_AUTONUMBER_COLLISION` exit is for a number "the engine ITSELF issued" — a number the driver issued through the member on a reader object now exits there too; an internal docblock, a follow-up touch. (ii) The changeset names the error-code change but not the HTTP status a REST caller sees on that exhausted path; `ERR_AUTONUMBER_COLLISION` carries `code` and `cause` and no `status`, exactly as on the engine-issued exit, so the seat confirms the envelope status in its prose-face ACCEPT if any page names 409 for it. (iii) The docs drift check lists `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx` and siblings that name `IDataDriver`; prose faces, the seat's ACCEPT.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-m25d8w`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FaVyM6YvQLg9CsjPVCYc5K`

**VERDICT: PASS**
